related_questions.question: Is Ohio getting rid of state income tax?

text_blocks.snippet: No, Ohio is not currently eliminating its state income tax. However, there is legislation being proposed to phase out the state income tax and the Commercial Activity Tax (CAT) by 2030. This would be done through a phased-in approach, reducing tax rates annually until reaching a full elimination.

list.title: Proposed Legislation:
list.snippet: Ohio lawmakers have introduced legislation to eliminate the state income tax and the CAT, a tax on business revenue, by 2030.

list.title: Phased-in Approach:
list.snippet: The plan is to gradually reduce income tax rates over time, eventually eliminating them completely by the end of the decade.

list.title: Economic Impact:
list.snippet: Supporters of the plan argue it will encourage businesses to relocate to Ohio and attract residents, while critics raise concerns about the potential impact on state revenue and the need to find alternative funding sources.

list.title: Regressive Concerns:
list.snippet: Some critics also point out that eliminating the income tax could disproportionately benefit higher earners and shift the tax burden to other forms of taxation, like sales taxes, which are considered more regressive.

list.title: Alternative Revenue Sources:
list.snippet: If the income tax is eliminated, Ohio would need to find alternative revenue sources to fund vital services like education and public safety, according to Policy Matters Ohio.

list.title: Current Situation:
list.snippet: While the legislation is proposed, it has not yet been passed. The current state income tax in Ohio has two brackets, with rates ranging from 2.75% to 3.5%.
